title: County growth context coincides with distinct federal trust patterns while civic action remains stable
source_unit: 2024 Cooperative Election Study common-content post-election respondent with county FIPS, linked to county 2020–2023 population change
geography: United States; 620 counties with at least 100,000 residents and valid 2020/2023 population estimates

observations.period: 2024; CES county population-change group Q1 lowest; 2020–2023 context

denominator.unit: CES respondents; 155 represented counties; place frame 155

federal_trust.unit: percent saying they trust the federal government a great deal or fair amount; commonpostweight

state_trust.unit: percent saying they trust state government a great deal or fair amount; commonpostweight

civic_action.unit: percent reporting at least one selected civic action; commonpostweight

reported_voted.unit: percent reporting definitely voted in November 2024; commonpostweight

observations.method: Weighted descriptive pooled CES common-content comparison using commonpostweight; county population change is split into four place-count quartiles among counties with at least 100,000 residents and usable 2020/2023 estimates.
observations.uncertainty: No complex-survey standard errors or county-representative estimates in this pass; county FIPS supplies context but respondents are not a county probability sample.
observations.subgroup: CES respondents linked to counties in the Q1 lowest population-change quartile.
observations.counterinterpretation: Population change includes births, deaths, domestic migration, and international migration; trust, civic action, and reported voting can reflect party identity, composition, selection, and question universe rather than local growth.

related_sources.claim: CES 2024 common-content public data supply county FIPS, trust, civic-action, vote, and commonpostweight fields.
Census county estimates supply 2020 and 2023 population context.
Reproduction script for county quartile assignment, valid universes, and weighted endpoints.

boundary: This is a county-context comparison, not a county-representative opinion estimate or a causal local-business, capacity, migration, trust, civic-action, or voting result. It does not measure belonging, fairness, attribution, service use, or the respondent’s material exposure; the CES growth layer must remain separate from the county capacity screen until a valid common geography, time, and respondent/place design is established.
